text: {"status":"unresolved","evidence_ids":["ev-07062184bfddb184c2c65f15"],"request_dft":true,"proposed_test_ids":["compute-li-fe-p-o-competing-phase-references"],"rationale":"The only record, ev-07062184bfddb184c2c65f15, is a converged PBE (no U) VASP relaxation of the olivine Li4Fe4P4O16 cell. It gives a total energy of -195.77 eV, a max force of 0.0096 eV/A, and a stress of 1.22 kbar, so it is a valid total-energy result for the target phase. A hull claim needs energy_above_hull, which depends on the energies of all competing Li-Fe-P-O phases, such as Li3PO4, Fe2O3, Fe3(PO4)2, FePO4, Li4P2O7, Fe2P, LiFeP2O7 and the elemental and oxide references. The record has reference_set_id null and reference_complete null, and no competing-phase energies appear in the evidence. A total energy alone cannot place the phase on or above the hull, so the record cannot decide the claim in either direction. Scope is also unspecified, which adds to the gap. Because the decisive step is a calculation (PBE energies of the competing phases computed consistently with the same settings), DFT could resolve it, and the competing-phase reference test addresses the visible gap. Other panelists have not spoken yet. If a later contribution calls this supported from the total energy or from literature knowledge that LFP is stable, I would dispute it. Literature values do not satisfy the evidence rules, and PBE without U handles Fe redox energetics poorly, so the outcome is not trivially known. A falsifying result would be a hull energy above 0 eV/atom when computed against a complete, consistent reference set. A caveat is that a threshold of exactly 0.0 is strict, so tolerance or numerical noise needs consideration. Competing-phase energies should use matched POTCARs, cutoff and magnetic ordering."}
